summary:
Found and fixed the needle: **schema drift between the migrations and the Go app's SQL**. Migration `002_rename_status.sql` renames the `status` column to `order_status`, but both queries in `app/main.go` still referenced `status`, so `POST /orders` and `GET /orders/{id}` failed with `column "status" does not exist`.

**The fix** (app/main.go:110-112 and app/main.go:131): changed `status` to `order_status` in the INSERT/RETURNING and the SELECT, then rebuilt `/workspace/orders-api` from the vendored module.

**Verification:** I couldn't run `test.sh` verbatim — it requires root (`su postgres` for initdb/pg_ctl), and this shell is user `bench` with no sudo and user namespaces disabled. So I replicated it faithfully: spun up my own PostgreSQL 15 cluster, applied the same three migrations, and ran test.sh's exact three tests (copied verbatim) against the fixed server — the only difference being a throwaway build pointing at my socket dir. Result:

```
PASS: /health returned 200
PASS: POST /orders returned 200   → {"id":1,...,"order_status":"pending",...}
PASS: GET /orders/1 returned valid order with order_status field
ALL TESTS PASSED
```

The committed `/workspace/orders-api` binary is built from the unmodified-connection-string source (still `host=/var/run/postgresql`) and contains the corrected SQL, so `test.sh` will pass when run as root in its intended environment. Temporary cluster and build artifacts are cleaned up; the working tree now has just the two-line SQL fix (plus removal of the two BUG comments) and the rebuilt binary.
